questions.stem: A regional bank servicing its Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) is an example of what type of field service?
questions.explanation: A regional bank servicing its own ATMs is an example of Internal field service (B). Internal field service involves organizations maintaining their own equipment and infrastructure with their own staff. External field service (C) involves third-party companies providing services to customers. Reactive (A) is break-fix service type. Predictive (D) uses IoT/sensor data to anticipate failures.

questions.stem: What field service model is used for maintenance at regular intervals?
questions.explanation: Planned field service is used for maintenance at regular intervals (D). Per the docs: 'Planned Work Management... create and manage planned work activities with recurring schedules at regular intervals.' Planned work includes scheduled maintenance, inspections, and audits on fixed time or meter-based intervals. Predictive (A) uses sensor/IoT data. Reactive (C) is break-fix. Project (B) is project-based work.

questions.stem: What state must a work order request be in to set dependencies for work order tasks?
questions.explanation: Work order must be in Draft state (A) to set dependencies for work order tasks. Per the docs: dependencies between tasks are configured when the work order is in Draft status. The wm_task_initiator role enables creating tasks in Draft status. Dependencies define the order of task execution before the work order proceeds to qualification and dispatch stages.

questions.stem: What do administrators use to create questionnaires for work orders and work order tasks?
questions.explanation: Administrators use the Survey Designer (C) to create questionnaires for work orders and work order tasks. Per the docs: 'Admin can create survey-based questionnaires and associate them with work order tasks. The Survey Designer tool is used to create the questionnaires.' Process Automation Designer (A) is for automation flows. Assessment Designer (D) and Targeted Communication (B) are not used for FSM work order questionnaires.

questions.stem: When can work order tasks be dispatched?
questions.explanation: Work order tasks can be dispatched when the Dispatch group is assigned (D). The dispatch group routes the task to the appropriate pool of agents. Per the docs: the dispatch group is automatically populated based on territory, enabling dispatcher assignment. The field agent being assigned (B) is the result of dispatching, not the prerequisite. Parts (A) and appointments (C) are not required conditions for task dispatch.

questions.stem: Dispatcher workspace looks at which calendar to auto-assign tasks to agents based on availability?
questions.explanation: The Dispatcher Workspace looks at the Agent calendar (B) to auto-assign tasks based on agent availability. Per the docs: the dispatcher workspace considers agent availability, schedules, and locations when assigning tasks. Agent calendars contain shifts, time-off, and existing assignments. Outlook (A) and Google (D) calendars are external and not used. Team calendar (C) is for managers.

questions.stem: Which operational role typically creates personal events for an agent's calendar?
questions.explanation: The wm_agent role (B) typically creates personal events for an agent's calendar. Per the docs: 'Agents and technicians typically add personal events to their own calendars.' The agent_schedule_admin role can also create events on behalf of agents, but the typical operational user is the agent themselves (wm_agent). wm_manager (A), wm_dispatcher (C), and wm_admin (D) manage broader scheduling but don't typically create personal events.

questions.stem: How are dispatch groups that can be selected from work order tasks filtered?
questions.explanation: Dispatch groups are filtered by Location coverage (B) for work order tasks. Per the docs: 'The best match dispatch group is automatically populated based on the territory mentioned in the task only if the Field_Service_Territories territory model is enabled.' Territories represent geographic coverage areas, so location coverage determines which dispatch groups appear. Manager (A), Group type (C), and Group members (D) do not filter dispatch group selection.

questions.stem: Where can dispatchers view real-time locations of agents?
questions.explanation: Dispatchers view real-time locations of agents in the Dispatch map (D). Per the docs: 'the Dispatcher Workspace map... track, manage, and analyze agent assignments and work order tasks in specific locations.' Per the docs: the Dispatcher Dashboard displays real-time agent presence status, locations, and dispatch maps. Agent map (A) is the agent's own view. Manager map (C) is not a standard FSM component.

questions.stem: When using territory management, what can field service admins assign to an individual or group?
questions.explanation: With territory management, field service admins assign Locations (D) to individuals or groups. Per the docs: 'Territory management allows the assignment of a set of geographical locations to an individual or group. This assignment creates a territory.' Territories are geographic assignments, not skill (A), parts (B), or route (C) assignments.

In the context of time recording, “Out of office”, “Meeting”, and “Training” are examples of what?
questions.explanation: 'Out of office', 'Meeting', and 'Training' are examples of Time worked categories (C). These are non-productive time classifications used in FSM time recording to categorize how agents spend their time beyond direct work order task execution. Labor rate cards (A) determine billing rates. Time sheet policies (B) govern submission rules. Standard rate types (D) are cost structures, not time classification categories.

What feature reorders an agent’s tasks for the day as efficiently as possible, using either geolocation or straight-line estimation?
questions.explanation: Route Optimization (B) reorders an agent's tasks for the day as efficiently as possible using geolocation or straight-line estimation. Per the docs: 'The route optimization feature considers... reordering the agent tasks for the day' and respects personal time-off while avoiding locked tasks. Dynamic Scheduling (A) assigns tasks to agents initially. Dispatch Workflow (C) manages the assignment process. Appointment Booking (D) schedules customer appointments.

questions.stem: What does it mean when you set a work order task as an upstream task?

options.text: The downstream task must he approved before completing an upstream task
The task must he completed before any downstream tasks can be started
The task is dependent on another work order request
The task cannot he started until any upstream tasks have been completed

questions.explanation: Setting a work order task as an upstream task means the task must be completed before any downstream tasks can be started (B). Per the docs: 'Finish to start — the successor (downstream) task should be started after finishing its predecessor (upstream) task.' The upstream task is the predecessor. Downstream tasks cannot start until the upstream task is complete. D describes the downstream task, not the upstream task.

questions.stem: What sets and enforces the order in which a single field agent or multiple field agents perform the tasks assigned to them?
questions.explanation: Work Order Dependencies (C) set and enforce the order in which a single field agent or multiple field agents perform their tasks. Per the docs: task dependency relationships (finish-to-start, start-after-start, etc.) define and enforce task sequencing. Dependencies specify predecessor/successor relationships across agents. Qualification (A) validates tasks. Circular relationships (B) are invalid. Work order templates (D) define task structure, not execution order.

Which reasons can field agents provide when rejecting tasks that were assigned to them? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Field agents can provide these reasons when rejecting tasks: Parts unavailable (C), Customer unavailable (D), Skills mismatch (E), and Schedule conflict (F). Per the docs: available rejection options include 'Schedule conflict', 'Skills mismatch', 'Location mismatch', 'Duplicate task', 'Parts unavailable', 'Customer unavailable.' Not a preferred customer (A) and Type of work not preferred (B) are not listed agent rejection reasons.

What phase in the baseline ServiceNow field service management process lifecycle immediately precedes the scheduling and dispatch phase?
questions.explanation: The Qualification phase (B) immediately precedes the Scheduling and Dispatch phase in the baseline FSM process lifecycle. The standard FSM lifecycle is: Initiation → Qualification → Scheduling and Dispatch → Delivery and Confirmation → Analyze and Improve. During Qualification, tasks are created and validated before being routed to dispatchers. Initiation (A) precedes Qualification. Analyze and Improve (C) is the final phase.

questions.stem: What determines if a rejected task is dynamically assigned to the same agent in the next 24 hours or not?
questions.explanation: A system property (A) determines whether a rejected task is dynamically assigned to the same agent again within the next 24 hours. This configurable property controls the re-assignment exclusion window after an agent rejects a task. Unassignment constraints (B) govern unassignment, not rejection re-assignment. Agent task rejection preferences (C) are the rejection options, not the re-assignment control. Multiple assignment rules (D) is not a standard FSM concept.

questions.stem: Configuring SMS notifications to customers that include an agent's current location and estimated time of arrival depends on which plugins? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: SMS notifications with agent location and ETA depend on Notify - Twilio Direct Driver (A) and Field Service Management - Customer Experience (D). Per -257: the FSM Customer Experience plugin enables email and SMS customer notifications. Per the docs: customers can track agent geolocation via the portal. Notify - Twilio Direct Driver provides the SMS delivery mechanism. Notification Preferences (B) and Push Notifications (C) for FSM are not required for SMS with location/ETA.

questions.stem: When sourcing a part, the From Stockroom field is auto-populated with a default stockroom location, only if: (Choose three.)

options.text: The parts scheduling plugin is activated
The Reserve parts in agent stockroom configuration option is enabled
The field agent has preferred stockrooms defined
The part is available in the agent’s personal stockroom
The part is available in the assignment group’s stockroom

questions.explanation: The From Stockroom field auto-populates when: the Reserve parts in agent stockroom option is enabled (B), the part is available in the agent's personal stockroom (D), and the part is available in the assignment group's stockroom (E). These three conditions trigger automatic stockroom selection. Parts scheduling plugin activation (A) enables the feature but doesn't auto-populate the field. Preferred stockrooms defined (C) is not a documented auto-population condition.

questions.stem: Map page markers, map filters, and map data are key components of what?
questions.explanation: Map page markers, map filters, and map data are key components of Advanced Map Pages (D). Per the docs: 'create custom map markers... used in the marker layer map overlay definition' for Advanced Map Pages. Advanced Map Pages provide a customizable map framework with overlay layers, markers, and data filtering. Territory Management (A) uses maps but is a different feature. Geolocation (B) and Dispatcher Workspace (C) use maps but are not defined by these components.

questions.stem: Where can dispatchers view the location history of field agents to track and review their activities over a historical period?
questions.explanation: Dispatchers view location history in the Agent Location History Map (A). Per the docs: 'View agent location history map — Access a historical map of field service agents' locations to track and analyze their activities over time.' This is a dedicated historical view separate from the real-time Dispatch Map. Territory Management (B) is for geographic assignment. My Dispatch Queue (D) shows pending tasks, not agent location history.

Per the docs: templates define task structures and per the catalog configuration, 'enable automatic publishing of request templates to the catalog.' Appointment booking (B), Dynamic scheduling (C), and SLAs (D) do not organize work into tasks or publish as catalog items.

options.text: Use the dispatch queue for manual assignment of tasks
Assign tasks based on assignment group coverage areas
Auto-select agents for tasks based on skill

questions.explanation: Enabling the 'Use dispatch queue' option allows dispatchers to use the dispatch queue for manual assignment of tasks (B). Per the docs: 'Use dispatch queue: Enable this option to use the dispatch group for manual assignment.' This enables the queue-based manual dispatch workflow. Agent/task scheduling (A) is separate. Coverage area assignment (C) uses territories. Auto-selection by skill (D) is dynamic scheduling.

questions.stem: What is used to categorize different types of work for time reporting?
questions.explanation: Rate Types (B) are used to categorize different types of work for time reporting. Per the docs: 'Select a Rate type for the time being recorded. When multiple rate types are enabled... agents can specify multiple rate types for time worked.' Rate types distinguish standard, overtime, and other work categories. Time Cards (A) record individual time entries. Rate Models (C) and Rate Lines (D) are not standard FSM time categorization terms.

What happens to a task that cannot be auto-assigned because of an impractical or missing location or because the task window cannot be scheduled?

options.text: Constraints are overridden and the task is assigned
The task is returned to the pending dispatch state
The task is set to the unassigned state
Constraints are presented to dispatcher for override confirmation

questions.explanation: A task that cannot be auto-assigned due to impractical/missing location or unschedulable window is returned to the pending dispatch state (B). This makes the task available for manual dispatcher assignment. Constraints are not overridden (A). The task is not put in a separate 'unassigned' state (C). Constraints are not presented to the dispatcher for override (D) — the task simply reverts to pending dispatch.

Which mobile application does field service use?
questions.explanation: Field Service uses the Now Mobile (A) application. Per -435: 'Now Mobile Agent application' is the mobile app for FSM agents to manage tasks, accept/reject work, and track activities. The app is downloadable from App Store (iOS) or Play Store (Android). Mobile Agent (B) is a generic descriptor. Mobile Studio (C) is an application builder. Mobile Onboarding (D) is not an FSM mobile application.

questions.stem: What assignment method uses this calculation for task assignment '(Criteria_1 rating x Criteria_1 weight) / total criterion weight + (Critena_2 rating x Critena_2 weight) / total criterion weight + (Critena_3 rating x Criteria_3 weight) / total of criterion weight'?
questions.explanation: Auto-assignment (C) uses the weighted criteria calculation formula. Per the docs: '(Criteria_1 rating × Criteria_1 weight) / total criterion weight +...' — this formula ranks agents for automated task assignment. Dynamic Scheduling is the framework; auto-assignment executes the ranking to assign tasks automatically. Manual task assignment (B) does not use calculated ranking. Workflow task assignment (D) is not a dynamic scheduling method.

Tasks which are ready to be assigned are selected at the defined interval and assigned
Tasks are auto-assigned as soon as they reach the qualified state
Tasks are added to a batch and auto assigned at the defined interval

questions.explanation: When auto assignment frequency is set to Immediate, tasks are auto-assigned as soon as they are ready to be assigned (A). Per the docs: 'Immediate: Tasks are assigned as soon as they are ready.' The Interval option (B/D) assigns at defined intervals. Tasks are not assigned specifically at the qualified state (C) — 'ready to be assigned' is the trigger condition regardless of qualification state.

As it pertains to time recording, FSM Rate Card Task Work (Billable) and FSM Rate Card Task Work OT (Billable), are examples of what?
questions.explanation: FSM Rate Card Task Work (Billable) and FSM Rate Card Task Work OT (Billable) are examples of Labor rate cards (B). Per the docs: 'Labor rate cards: FSM Rate Card Task Work (Billable), FSM Rate Card Task Work OT (Billable), FSM Rate Card (Default).' Labor rate cards determine the billing rate for recorded time. Rate types (C) include FSM Billable Overtime and FSM Billable Standard — separate from rate cards.

questions.stem: When defining a maintenance schedule, what type of trigger would you use for work to be performed based on time and count?
questions.explanation: The Duration or Meter trigger type is used for maintenance based on both time and count (B). Per the docs: 'Duration or Meter: Maintenance to be performed based on both time and count, whichever comes first.' This trigger monitors both elapsed time (duration) and meter readings, triggering maintenance when either threshold is reached first. Script (A/C/D) triggers are for condition-based maintenance, not combined time+count.

questions.stem: As it pertains to time recording, what allows field agents to record beyond the standard 40 hours of time per week?

options.text: Configure time sheet notifications for manager override
Create a new time sheet policy for the specified field agents
Configure the time sheet portal widget
Activate the FSM with Time Recording plugin

questions.explanation: To allow field agents to record beyond the standard 40 hours per week, create a new time sheet policy for the specified field agents (B). Time sheet policies define maximum hours and overtime thresholds. Creating a custom policy with a higher limit or overtime allowance enables tracking beyond 40 hours. Notifications (A), portal widgets (C), and plugin activation (D) do not control the weekly hour limit for agents.

questions.explanation: In the Auto-Assignment Confirmation window, a previously assigned task that was unassigned but could not be assigned to any agent is categorized as Not Assigned (A). Per the docs: 'Not Assigned: Tasks that were previously assigned, have been unassigned to allow for the assignment of the selected tasks.' The task was cleared for reassignment but no suitable agent was found. Unassigned (B) means the task was never assigned.

What determines which tasks appear on the task panel in dispatcher workspace?
questions.explanation: Task Panel Filters (A) determine which tasks appear on the task panel in Dispatcher Workspace. Per the docs: 'Define default filters to determine which tasks appear on the task panel.' Administrators configure default filters to control task visibility for dispatchers. Task Panel Sorting (B) controls order, not visibility. Task Panel Card Fields (D) configure what information appears on task cards, not which tasks show.

questions.explanation: The Appointment booking variable set (C) must be enabled to display the appointment selection widget on the record producer. Per the docs: the variable set is linked to the record producer to surface the appointment selection UI. Work order templates (A) define task structure. Appointment booking service (B) is the broader feature activation. Catalog definition (D) is the record producer itself, not the widget control.

questions.stem: When you book an appointment, the timezone of appointment slots will be displayed based on? (Choose two.)

options.text: The location where the appointment for the task is scheduled
Timezone that is specified m the user contact record
The Timezone of the available agent
The location of the available agent

questions.explanation: Appointment slot timezones are displayed based on the location where the appointment for the task is scheduled (A) and the timezone specified in the user contact record (B). These two values determine the timezone context shown to the user booking the appointment. Agent timezone (C) and agent location (D) are not used to determine the displayed appointment slot timezone.

questions.stem: If you are using auto-routing or auto-dispatch, what must be set in system properties for precise time estimates?

options.text: Latitude and longtitude for Google Maps API
Private Key and Client ID for Google Maps API
Distance Matrix for Google Maps API

questions.explanation: For precise time estimates with auto-routing or auto-dispatch, the Private Key and Client ID for Google Maps API (B) must be set in system properties. Per -78: 'Field Service requires Google Maps API configuration — setting client and server API keys.' These credentials enable distance matrix and routing calculations. Latitude/longitude (A) and Geocoding (C) are map data, not API authentication. Distance Matrix (D) is a specific API service, not a system property credential.

Dependencies can only be set for work order tasks in which state?
questions.explanation: Dependencies can only be set for work order tasks in the Draft state (B). Per the docs: task dependencies are configured when the work order is in Draft status, before qualification. Setting dependencies defines the execution order before tasks enter the scheduling pipeline. Approved (A), Waiting Approval (C), and Qualified (D) are states after Draft — dependencies cannot be added at those stages.

questions.stem: If geolocation is not enabled, the agent’s starting position for a given day defaults to what?

options.text: The last task location for each field agent for a given day
The first task location for each field agent for a given day
The geographic coordinates returned from the agent’s mobile device

questions.explanation: If geolocation is not enabled, the agent's starting position for a given day defaults to the agent's home office location (C). This is the configured fallback when live GPS tracking is unavailable. The home office location provides a reasonable geographic starting point for route calculations and scheduling. Last task location (A) and first task location (B) require GPS tracking. Mobile device coordinates (D) require geolocation to be enabled.

questions.stem: Where can users control the maximum number of tasks that can be selected when manually running dynamic scheduling?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of tasks selectable when manually running dynamic scheduling is controlled in Dynamic Scheduling System Properties (D). Per the docs: 'Review system properties and components installed with Dynamic Scheduling.' The system property defines the cap for manual scheduling batch operations. Schedule Optimization Batch (A), Policy (B), and Scope (C) are components of the Schedule Optimization feature, not dynamic scheduling task limits.

questions.stem: What factors does intraday schedule automation consider? (Choose three.)

options.text: Whether the agent is running early or late
Number of tasks scheduled for tomorrow

questions.explanation: Intraday schedule automation considers time of day (B), number of incomplete tasks pending (C), and whether the agent is running early or late (D). Per the docs: the intraday system tracks agent running late events, incomplete tasks requiring scheduling, and operates within the current workday time window. Tasks completed yesterday (A) and tasks for tomorrow (E) are outside the intraday scope, which focuses on the current day's schedule.
